title: Bounded-below closed-support right adjoint and its fixed adjunction
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Work in the ordinary bounded-below derived categories $D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of small-etale $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $i_*$ for the right derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], which agrees with exact closed direct image. Define $i^!$ to be the chosen right adjoint of $i_*$, with its fixed adjunction $i_*\dashv i^!$, its unit and its counit. This is the bounded-below closed-support adjoint of [lem-exc-closed-ambient], obtained by deriving the supported inverse image $F\mapsto i^{-1}\ker(F\to j_*j^{-1}F)$ for the open complement $j$ [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel]. Equip $i^!$ with the cohomological-shift comparison obtained as the adjunction mate of the direct-image shift comparison. The right adjoint is chosen by its adjunction universal property, not as an unspecified functor.

proof.text: Construction and underived obligation. Set $S(F)=i^{-1}\ker(F\to j_*j^{-1}F)$, using the kernel functor of [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel] with its induced $A$-action. The canonical Hom bijection and exactness in [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction] lift from abelian sheaves to constant-$A$ modules as follows. For each $a\in A$, naturality of that bijection identifies $S(a_F)g$ with $g a_G$ precisely when $a_F f=f i_*(a_G)$; hence it restricts to a bijection on $A$-linear maps, in both directions. Constant-ring sheaf linearity can be checked on constant scalars, since general local scalars are locally constant and the equalities glue. Kernels and cokernels in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] have their underlying abelian-sheaf kernels and sheafified cokernels, so the forgetful functor creates and reflects exactness. The exact abelian closed direct image therefore gives exact module direct image. This constructs the additive sheaf adjunction $i_*\dashv S$, rather than choosing an unknown right-adjoint object.

proof.text: Derived object and morphisms. The module categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Define $i^!=RS$ by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], with its derived-functor comparison. Concretely choose $K\cong QI_K$ with $I_K$ bounded below injective, using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], and put $i^!K=Q(SI_K)$. Represent a morphism by its unique homotopy class $I_K\to I_L$ using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], and apply $S$ termwise. Additivity preserves homotopies, identities and composition. The derived-functor universal property gives independence of representatives and its unique comparison isomorphisms. If $I_K^r=0$ for $r<b$, then $(SI_K)^r=S(0)=0$ there, so the output lies in $D^+$; no finite cohomological-dimension bound is required.

Fixed derived adjunction. Exactness of $i_*$ makes its derived direct image the termwise functor. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], $C(i_*)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. For bounded below $M$ choose a quasi-isomorphism $s:M\to I$ to a bounded below injective complex [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]; naturality of $\alpha$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives $Ri_*(Qs)\circ\alpha_M=\alpha_I\circ Q(i_*s)$, and $\alpha_I$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective](2), so $\alpha_M:Q(i_*M)\to Ri_*(QM)$ is an isomorphism. The exact-left-adjoint obligation from Step 1 lets [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] apply to $i_*\dashv S$, so $SI_K$ is K-injective. For bounded below $M$ the natural bijection is the composite
$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T,A)}(Q(i_*M),QI_K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(T,A)}(i_*M,I_K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(Z,A)}(M,SI_K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z,A)}(QM,Q(SI_K))$.
The outer bijections are [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; the middle one is [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Define the unit to be the image of $1_{i_*M}$ and the counit to be the inverse image of $1_{i^!K}$ under this bijection. Its inverse laws and naturality give the triangle identities. This fixes the adjunction attached to the constructed functor. This constructs the bounded-below closed-support adjunction required in the definition.

proof.text:
Shift data. On complexes the exact additive $F=i_*$ has $\tau_{M,n}:F(M[n])\cong F(M)[n]$, with identity components: the differentials agree because $F((-1)^n d)=(-1)^nF(d)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] these descend to the shift isomorphisms $\sigma$ of the triangulated functor $F_D$, compatible with $\varphi$; as $F_D$ preserves $D^+$, transport $\sigma$ along the isomorphisms $\alpha_M\circ\varphi_M$ of Step 3 to $e_{X,n}:Ri_*(X[n])\cong Ri_*(X)[n]$ on $D^+$, which obey zero and addition coherence. For $G=i^!$ and the fixed unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ of Step 3, equip $G$ with the structure of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique](iii). Explicitly its inverse comparison $G(K)[n]\to G(K[n])$ is
$G(\varepsilon_K[n])\circ G(e_{GK,n})\circ\eta_{(GK)[n]}$.
That node guarantees invertibility, coherence, and compatibility with this actual unit and counit; its uniqueness clause fixes the mate normalization. Thus every data component is constructed from kernels, injective resolutions and the specified adjunction.
